title: Lumbar FSU and isolated disc axial compressive stiffness at the initial reference test and after each 6DOF test direction
condition: intact FSU and isolated disc; loading-history (sequence) effect

quantity.name: axial compressive stiffness (reference compression test)
quantity.definition: slope of the loading branch (final of 8 cycles at 0.1 Hz) over 70-90% of max stress (0.77-1 MPa equivalent nucleus pressure); measured at the start (control) and after each single-DOF test. Hexapod robot coordinate system aligned to the specimen; displacements/rotations of the upper vertebra relative to the fixed lower vertebra about the disc centre of rotation (determined from axial and lateral radiographs); hybrid position/load control drives the primary axis while minimising the 5 off-axis forces/moments to zero.

source.authors: Amin DB, Lawless IM, Sommerfeld D, Stanley RM, Ding B, Costi JJ
source.sample: 14 lumbar FSUs (text: L1-2 x5, L2-3 x3, L3-4 x4, L4-5 x2); Thompson grade 3 n=5, 4 n=6, 5 n=3; human cadaveric lumbar FSUs, tested intact then as isolated disc (facets cut in a wedge); mean (SD) disc area 1775.4 (278.1) mm2, height 8.83 (1.92) mm

protocol.summary: Specimens in 37 C PBS with protease inhibitors; 12 h equilibration at a compressive load equivalent to 0.1 MPa nucleus pressure; follower preload equivalent to 0.5 MPa nucleus pressure during all 6DOF tests (external stress = nucleus pressure/1.5, applied to unloaded disc area 0.84*AP*LAT). Reference compression: ramp to 0.5 MPa-equivalent follower preload under 6DOF load control (off-axis loads zero), then 8 haversine cycles at 0.1 Hz of 0.6 MPa amplitude (peak 1.1 MPa, standing). Performed initially and after each of 12 DOF tests (order: LLS, RLS, AS, PS, LAR, RAR, LLB, RLB, Flex, Ext, combined flex-ext, compression), whole sequence first on intact FSU then on isolated disc (~64 h per specimen).
how_to_simulate: Model the FSU at rest (no prior loading history); fix the lower vertebra; apply a follower compressive load = (0.5/1.5 MPa) x disc area (0.84*AP*LAT)
Cycle the axial compression between 0.5 and 1.1 MPa equivalent nucleus pressure at 0.1 Hz with off-axis loads zero; use the 8th cycle
Compute the slope over 0.77-1.0 MPa (x area /1.5 to get force) and compare with 'Control (initial)'; repeat with facets removed for the isolated-disc value
Optional (poroelastic models): reproduce the test sequence to compare the drift of compressive stiffness after shear, rotation and bending tests
protocol.notes: Coordinate/reference: Hexapod robot coordinate system aligned to the specimen; displacements/rotations of the upper vertebra relative to the fixed lower vertebra about the disc centre of rotation (determined from axial and lateral radiographs); hybrid position/load control drives the primary axis while minimising the 5 off-axis forces/moments to zero. Table gives mean +- 95% CI; sd derived as CI_half/2.160*sqrt(14) (t(0.975,13)). Intact vs disc not significantly different (p=0.701). Compressive modulus (MPa) and phase angle also in Table 1 (not extracted). Same 14 specimens as Amin 2016b (J Orthop Res); the paper's level counts differ slightly between the two papers (JB text 5/3/4/2 vs JOR Table 1 4/4/4/2).
